analyst_view.overall: The Seville derby: Sevilla (6th, 18 pts, one win in five) host Betis (4th, 26 pts) at the Pizjuán at 18:30 on Saturday, with Betis away in Europe on Tuesday. Sevilla's 24-man squad has Peque and Fofana back, but Alfon, Carmona (both in the numbers), Marcão and Miguel Sierra are out, and García Plaza has said he will likely swap a striker for a third midfielder. Betis' squad has Cucho Hernández back from injury, Riquelme and Bellerín included and Bernal available after a four-match ban, while Ceballos and Morante are out (in the numbers). José María Sánchez Martínez referees, as the numbers assumed, and the numbers already add a large derby boost to cards. On match day the clubs' squad lists still stand: Peque, Fofana and Rubén Vargas are in Sevilla's 24 and Cucho and Bernal in Betis' 23; one English preview listing Peque as injured and Bernal as banned is out of date against those lists, so the view is unchanged.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and already take off Morante and Ceballos for Betis. Cucho is back in the squad and Peque returns for Sevilla, but Sevilla lose centre-back Marcão and plan a more cautious three-man midfield; these offset, so I stay at 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners and already take some off Sevilla for their low recent count (19 in six). García Plaza's extra midfielder may mean less wide play, but Peque's return and Betis' wingers Antony and Abde keep both flanks busy; nothing clear moves it, so 9.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.7 cards, already including a large derby boost (about +39%) and Sánchez Martínez's record of about 4.5 cards a game. Bernal, a combative midfielder, is back from his ban, but the heat of a Seville derby is exactly what the boost already counts, so I add nothing and stay at 6.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.4 shots and already add Betis' busy recent shooting (97 in six) and Sevilla conceding plenty. Sevilla's coach plans to drop a striker for a third midfielder, which should slow the game a little, but Peque is back, so I trim only slightly, to about 26.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target and already add Betis' good recent accuracy. A more cautious Sevilla shape pulls down a little, but Cucho and Riquelme, who scored three in his last two games, are both in Betis' squad; these offset, so I stay at 9.2.
